newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal allots PLN 11.5 mln to buyback.
newsitem.headline: Universal allots PLN 11.5 mln to buyback.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish trader Universal SA on Thursday lifted to 11.5 million from 1.5 million zlotys the share of last year's net profit to buy back shares and retire them, the firm's spokeswoman said.

"During the shareholders meeting a proposal was put to increase the amount for buying back shares to 11.5 million zlotys....The proposal by (Britain's) Servepart Ltd was accepted nearly unanimuously," Agnieszka Szostek told Reuters.
Universal, which has 23,100,510 shares outstanding, made a 23-million-zloty net profit last year.

Szostek said the buyback operation on the bourse could last the rest of the year and that once all the shares were bought back the firm would hold another shareholders meeting to pass a resolution to retire them. @
Szostek said the rest of last year's profit would be put into reserve capital.
Universal has said it seeks to buy back and retire shares in order to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) representing 9.78 percent of its shares in public trade.
Universal's ADR issue, already approved by the U.S.'s Securities and Exchange Commission, would be the fourth by a Polish company following listings by Mostostal Export, Stalexport and Bank Gdanski.
Servepart holds a 17.5-percent stake in Universal.
